task_paradigm: Mechanosensory trigger-hair afferent to giant motor neuron mandible release
evidence: Measured sensorimotor latency; circuit power from SUB004
source: Gronenberg (1995) J. Comp. Physiol. A 176:391-404; Patek et al. (2006) PNAS 103:12787-12792; SUB004
note: Neural sensorimotor trigger latency is ~5.1 ms (0.625 ms conduction + 4.5 ms synaptic/trigger release in SUB004); elastic mechanical mandible closure takes 0.126 ms.

task_paradigm: Coriolis-force campaniform sensilla electrotonic reflex to b1 wing-steering muscle
power_scope: Haltere sensorimotor feedback loop + steering muscle actuation (SUB005)
evidence: Measured electrotonic reflex latency; loop power from SUB005
source: Hengstenberg (1998) Nature 392:757-758; Frye & Dickinson (2001) Neuron 32:385; Dickerson et al. (2019) Curr. Biol. 29:3517; SUB005
note: Monosynaptic electrotonic feedback stabilizes pitch/roll in 3-5 ms (4.67 ms in SUB005, 2.34 uJ/correction). Paper 3 Table 1 used 0.1 mW (0.5 uJ) by excluding steering actuation.

plain_name: Teleost fish Mauthner vs. non-Mauthner escape
task_paradigm: Short-latency Mauthner C-start (SLC) vs. long-latency non-Mauthner MiD3cm escape (LLC)
power_scope: Whole adult teleost CNS (~0.1 g, NEU11)
evidence: Measured SLC/LLC escape latencies; adult teleost CNS power from NEU11
source: Korn & Faber (2005) Neuron 47:13-28; Burgess & Granato (2007) J. Neurosci. 27:4984-4994; Kohashi & Oda (2008) J. Neurosci. 28:10641-10653; NEU11
note: Burgess & Granato (2007) report mean SLC latency 5.3 ms (Mauthner single spike, stereotyped escape) vs. LLC mean 28 ms (non-Mauthner reticulospinal population grading escape trajectory). Larval 6 ug brain alone is ~0.1 uW.

task_paradigm: 4-methylcyclohexanol (MCH) odor-intensity discrimination in 7 mm decision chamber
power_scope: Whole adult insect CNS metabolic budget (NEU07; ~0.15 mg brain)
evidence: Measured reaction times & DDM decomposition; CNS power from NEU07
source: DasGupta, Ferreira & Miesenbock (2014) Science 344:901-904; Groschner et al. (2018) Cell 173:894-905; Placais & Preat (2013) Science 339:440; NEU07
note: Groschner et al. (2018) decompose chamber RT into 1.296 s non-decision walking transit plus ~0.20 s (high-contrast) to ~1.10 s (narrow-contrast) pure alpha-beta_c Kenyon-cell Shal/FoxP integration. Varying odor ratio (0.1 to 0.9) is a difficulty sweep (~96% fast on easy vs. ~60-85% slow on hard), so fast_accuracy_pct is omitted to avoid conflating stimulus contrast with fixed-task SAT.

task_paradigm: Color-similar artificial flower foraging: water distractors (fast) vs. 0.12% quinine penalty (deliberative)
power_scope: Whole bumblebee CNS (~1.2 mg brain; ~9.6e5 neurons)
evidence: Measured within-individual quinine accuracy shift (p=0.004) & hover decision times; isolated brain respirometry scaling
source: Chittka, Dyer, Bock & Dornhaus (2003) Nature 424:388; Dyer & Chittka (2004) J. Comp. Physiol. A 190:759-763; Tait et al. (2024) J. Exp. Biol. 227:jeb247335
note: Chittka et al. (2003) measured exact within-bee accuracy jump from 62.0% (+/-11.2% SD, plain water distractors) to 83.0% (0.12% quinine penalty), reverting to 61.4% upon quinine removal. Whole-body thoracic flight power during flower hovering is ~0.050 W (~25 mJ to 70 mJ locomotor cost).

task_paradigm: Buzzer-enforced olfactory sampling window on close binary odor mixtures
power_scope: Whole awake mouse brain (0.42 g, CNS018; CMRglc)
evidence: Measured forced-sampling SAT curve & awake rodent brain CMRglc
source: Rinberg, Koulakov & Gelperin (2006) Neuron 51:351-358; Abraham et al. (2004) Neuron 44:865-876; Hyder et al. (2013) PNAS 110:3549-3554
note: Direct experimenter-controlled olfactory SAT: forcing early port withdrawal (~200 ms, 1 sniff) degrades binary-mixture discrimination toward ~62%, whereas 600 ms sampling reaches asymptotic ~88% accuracy.

task_paradigm: Bilateral Poisson click-train rate discrimination (0.10 s short stream vs. 1.00 s full integration)
power_scope: Whole awake rat brain (2.0 g, CNS019 / NEU16; CMRglc)
evidence: Measured chronometric/psychometric click accumulation & awake rat CMRglc
source: Brunton, Botvinick & Brody (2013) Science 340:95-98; Hyder et al. (2013) PNAS 110:3549-3554; NEU16
note: Brunton et al. (2013) show noiseless accumulator memory (tau > 1 s) across 0.1-1.0 s Poisson click streams. Whole-brain power matches NEU16 (0.12 W); Paper 3 Table 1 used 0.015 W regional cortical estimate.

plain_name: Macaque cued visual search & motion SAT
task_paradigm: Color-cued Fast-deadline vs. Accurate-cued visual search in frontal eye field (FEF)
power_scope: Whole awake macaque brain (87 g, CNS026; PET/autoradiographic CMRglc)
evidence: Measured single-unit FEF behavioral SAT & awake macaque CMRglc
source: Heitz & Schall (2012) Neuron 76:616-628; Hanks, Kiani & Shadlen (2014) eLife 3:e02260; Roitman & Shadlen (2002) J. Neurosci. 22:9475-9489; Kennedy et al. (1978) PNAS 75:4598-4602
note: Heitz & Schall (2012) measured exact mean RT 271 ms (~70% accuracy) under Fast cue vs. 614 ms (~90% accuracy) under Accurate cue on identical T/L arrays; Hanks et al. (2014) similarly found +168 ms RT elongation from high-speed to high-accuracy RDM regime. NEU19 lists 6.5 W upper bound.

task_paradigm: Delayed multimodal abstract same/different rule switching in nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL)
power_scope: Whole awake corvid brain (~10 g; avian CMRglc 27.3 umol/100g/min)
evidence: Measured trial delay + choice RT & accuracy; awake avian brain CMRglc
source: Veit & Nieder (2013) Nat. Commun. 4:2878; von Eugen, Tabrik, Gunturkun & Strockens (2022) Curr. Biol. 32:4306-4313
note: Crows hold sample across 1.0 s Delay 1 + 0.5 s rule cue + 1.0 s Delay 2 + ~0.55 s choice peck (<1.2 s limit), achieving 90.8% (Bird P) and 91.1% (Bird D) accuracy. Power derived from von Eugen et al. (2022) awake avian brain glucose budget (13.1 mW/g; 3x lower per neuron than mammals).

task_paradigm: Spontaneous two-step metatool problem: impulsive short-stick probing vs. pre-action visual inspection
power_scope: Whole awake crow brain (7.5 g, CNS014; avian CMRglc 13.1 mW/g)
evidence: Measured probe/inspection durations & spontaneous first-trial success; avian brain CMRglc
source: Taylor, Hunt, Holzhaider & Gray (2007) Curr. Biol. 17:1504-1507; von Eugen et al. (2022) Curr. Biol. 32:4306-4313; CNS014
note: In Taylor et al. (2007), impulsive short-stick probing (~3.9 s/probe) yields 0% extraction, whereas pre-solution inspection (29.6 +/- 4.4 s in component group) yields 4/7 (57.1%) spontaneous error-free first-trial extraction (6/7 = 85.7% overall). Replaces unverified 8.0 s / 18%->84% values in Paper 3 draft; NEU15 listed 1.8 W whole-body-like power.

plain_name: Rock ant colony quorum nest-site choice
task_paradigm: Colony emigration to superior nest: harsh emergency low-quorum vs. benign deliberative high-quorum
power_scope: Whole emigrating colony metabolic rate (~180 workers, ~0.18 g biomass)
evidence: Measured colony decision durations & good-nest selection accuracy; ant respirometry scaling
source: Franks, Dornhaus, Fitzsimmons & Stevens (2003) Proc. R. Soc. B 270:2457-2463; Pratt & Sumpter (2006) PNAS 103:15906-15910; Lighton (1987) Physiol. Zool. 60:524
note: Pratt & Sumpter (2006) report emergency forced emigration in ~87 min (5,220 s) at 65% good-nest accuracy vs. unforced deliberative quorum emigration in ~565 min (33,900 s) at 90% accuracy, matching Franks et al. (2003) harsh vs. benign quorum shift. Aggregate CNS-only power of 180 workers (~4.5e7 neurons) is ~0.045 mW.

task_paradigm: 5-site nest-box choice (one 40-L excellent cavity vs. four 15-L mediocre cavities) via waggle-dance + stop-signal quorum
power_scope: Whole thermoregulating swarm cluster (~10,000-50,000 bees, ORG07)
evidence: Measured 5-trial field choice accuracy & cumulative dance duration; swarm power from ORG07
source: Seeley & Buhrman (2001) Behav. Ecol. Sociobiol. 49:416-427; Seeley et al. (2012) Science 335:108-111; ORG07
note: Swarms chose the single 40-L cavity in 4 of 5 field trials (80.0% accuracy) over ~16 h (57,600 s) cumulative scout deliberation despite mediocre 15-L boxes being discovered hours earlier. Active scout cohort (~300-500 flying scouts) consumes ~5 W (~2.88e5 J); aggregate scout CNS alone (~4e8 neurons) is ~0.1 W (~5.8e3 J).

task_paradigm: Speed-stressed vs. accuracy-instructed 2AFC lexical/perceptual discrimination (very-low-frequency items)
power_scope: Whole awake human brain (1,400 g, 8.6e10 neurons, NEU20 / CNS032)
evidence: Measured Experiment 1 RTs & error rates; human whole-brain CMRglc/CMRO2
source: Wagenmakers, Ratcliff, Gomez & McKoon (2008) J. Mem. Lang. 58:140-159; Ratcliff & McKoon (2008) Neural Comput. 20:873-922; Forstmann et al. (2008) PNAS 105:17538; Herculano-Houzel (2011) PLoS ONE 6:e17514
note: Exact Experiment 1 VLF word table values from Wagenmakers et al. (2008): Speed instruction 525 ms correct RT at 29.1% error (70.9% accuracy) vs. Accuracy instruction 674 ms at 14.7% error (85.3% accuracy). Simple perceptual choices (~0.35 s at 20 W) expend ~7.0 J.

plain_name: Human System-1 intuition vs. System-2 reflection
task_paradigm: Two-response cognitive reflection (conflict bat-and-ball problem: <4 s deadline + load vs. free deliberation)
power_scope: Whole awake human brain (20.0 W, NEU20)
evidence: Measured two-response initial vs. final accuracy & response window; whole-brain metabolic power
source: Bago & De Neys (2019) Thinking & Reasoning 25:257-299; Bago & De Neys (2017) Cognition 158:90-109; Herculano-Houzel (2011) PLoS ONE 6:e17514
note: Under strict 4 s initial response deadline + dot-matrix load, conflict bat-and-ball initial accuracy is up to 20.1% (~3.5 s), rising to up to 37.8% given unconstrained System-2 reflection (~15-20 s).

task_paradigm: Multi-step competition mathematics problem solving (AIME 15 problems in 180 min exam)
power_scope: Whole awake human brain (20.0 W, NEU20)
evidence: Standardized MAA AIME exam time budget & qualifier mean score; whole-brain CMRglc
source: Mathematical Association of America (2024) AIME Summary Statistics; Herculano-Houzel (2016) The Human Advantage (MIT Press); NEU20
note: 180-minute exam / 15 integer-answer problems = 600 s mean deliberation budget per problem (12,000 J at 20 W whole-brain power), matching Paper 3 Section 4.2 human reasoning anchor (~5.3/15 = 35.3% mean accuracy among top-5% AMC qualifiers).

plain_name: Frontier MoE LLM: single-pass vs. RL chain-of-thought
species_or_hardware: DeepSeek-V3 vs. DeepSeek-R1 (671B/37B MoE on 8x Nvidia H100 SXM5)
task_paradigm: AIME 2024 mathematics benchmark: single-pass direct answer (DeepSeek-V3) vs. extended RL CoT (DeepSeek-R1)
power_scope: 8x Nvidia H100 SXM5 GPU TDP (8 x 700 W = 5,600 W, SUB009)
evidence: Published AIME 2024 Pass@1 benchmarks & token lengths on 8xH100 node
source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) arXiv:2501.12948 / Nature (2025); Nvidia H100 Architecture Whitepaper (2022, SUB009)
note: Identical 671B-total / 37B-active MoE base architecture: single-pass DeepSeek-V3 scores 39.2% Pass@1 (~600 tokens at ~80 tok/s = 7.5 s, 42 kJ GPU TDP), while RL-trained DeepSeek-R1 scores 79.8% Pass@1 (~12,000 reasoning tokens = 150 s, 840 kJ GPU TDP; ~1.53 MJ at 10.2 kW full DGX H100 server wall power).

plain_name: Frontier reasoning LLM: GPT-4o single-pass vs. OpenAI o1
species_or_hardware: OpenAI GPT-4o vs. OpenAI o1 (8x Nvidia H100 SXM5 node equivalent)
task_paradigm: AIME 2024 mathematics benchmark: GPT-4o single-pass vs. o1 extended test-time reasoning
power_scope: 8x Nvidia H100 SXM5 GPU TDP (8 x 700 W = 5,600 W, SUB009)
evidence: Published OpenAI o1 System Card AIME 2024 Pass@1; 8xH100 TDP hardware reference
source: OpenAI (2024) OpenAI o1 System Card (arXiv:2412.16720); Snell et al. (2024) arXiv:2408.03314; SUB009
note: OpenAI o1 System Card reports AIME 2024 single-sample Pass@1 rising from 9.3% (GPT-4o, ~250 tokens in ~2.5 s = 14 kJ) to 74.4% (o1 single-sample, ~8,000-10,000 reasoning tokens in ~120 s = 672 kJ at 5.6 kW GPU TDP, or 83.3% with 64-sample consensus). Directly anchors Paper 3 Section 4.2 (6.72e5 J vs. 12 kJ human = 56x energy gap).
